statement: For the nine-variable real circle/contact incidence system, the real count fails to be locally constant exactly on arrangements having one of: a common real tangent line; a common real point; a real singular point of one conic lying on a circle tangent to the other two; a real tangency between two conics; or a common real tangent circle with matching curvature and equally directed normals at one contact.

answer.text: Five types: common tangent line; common point; singular-point contact; conic tangency; curvature-matched circle contact
answer.display: Five types: common tangent line; common point; singular-point contact; conic tangency; curvature-matched circle contact
answer.qualification: Real circle/contact incidence discriminant with the source’s orientation and admissibility conventions.

scope: Real parameter space of triples of plane conics in the nine-variable circle/contact-point formulation.
notes: This characterizes the discriminant; it does not classify all complementary real chambers.
